Another big problem is making the hardware work. In suburbia, you usually won't get decent reception on access points more than one house over with stock antennas on 2.4 and 5.8 ghz bands. If you had lower frequencies that carried better (like the 900 MHz ISM band) or a single elevated station that people could see and point a directional at, things would get better fast. You'd add a hop to a link if you went through an elevated point, but it might really be worth it. Unfortunately there's little to no modern hardware on the market that will easily let you add a directional antenna (it's fairly easy to add an external mount for the 5.8 ghz band antenna on a Linksys e3000 but those aren't made any more and usually hard to find).

So yeah, you would need either really good coverage of a neighborhood or to have more specialized hardware for it to work at all.
